passage:
On Monday morning the class buzzed about Saturday's birthday outing. Karthik listened from his desk. Nobody had said his name, and nobody had said “not you” either. That was the thing. Sunaina posted a group photo, the whole row of friends squeezed together, twelve people tagged. Karthik scrolled through the tags twice. His name wasn't there, and it hadn't been last time either.

At lunch he sat at the end of the bench and nobody moved over. When they stood up to leave, nobody looked back to see if he was coming. Walking to the bus he replayed everything he had said that week. Maybe he was too quiet. Maybe his jokes were boring. Maybe something about him was just wrong.

qa.q: How many people were tagged in Sunaina's group photo?
qa.a: Twelve people were tagged in Sunaina's group photo.

qa.q: How was Karthik feeling on the walk to the bus?
qa.a: Karthik felt hurt and left out, and began doubting himself, replaying everything he had said that week and wondering whether something was wrong with him.

qa.q: What small step could help Karthik that does not depend on that group?
qa.a: Karthik could ask one person in class for a small plan, join an activity built on a shared interest, or tell a trusted adult about feeling left out.

qa.q: How might Sunaina see the photo and the tags?
qa.a: Sunaina probably thought of it as an ordinary post about a fun day and did not think about who was missing.

grounding: A teenager is not openly bullied but is never invited, tagged or waited for, and gradually starts to think something is wrong with them.

“You're home early,” Jomon bhaiya said, looking up from his laptop. “No cricket?”

“Nobody waited for me at the gate,” Lalit said, dropping the bag. “They all left.”

“Maybe they forgot.”

“They always forget.” Lalit stared at the floor. “I'm not in the group chat, you know. Not since Class 8.”

“Since the group started?”

“No idea. I just never got the message.” Lalit's voice went small. “Maybe I'm boring.”

Jomon shut the laptop. “You're not boring. Last night you made Amma laugh so hard she spilled the tea.”

“That doesn't count. Amma has to laugh.”

“Okay, then come to my practice on Saturday. My friends like new faces.”

Lalit shrugged, but did not say no.

qa.q: Since which class has Lalit not been in the group chat?
qa.a: Lalit has not been in the group chat since Class 8.

qa.q: What does Lalit mean by saying, “Maybe I'm boring”?
qa.a: Lalit feels ignored and is starting to believe something is wrong with Lalit personally.

qa.q: What did Jomon offer Lalit as a next step?
qa.a: Jomon invited Lalit to come to practice on Saturday, where friends like new faces.

qa.q: How might Jomon have felt hearing that nobody waited for Lalit at the gate?
qa.a: Jomon probably felt concerned and protective, choosing gentle words and a practical invitation.

grounding: A teenager is never invited, tagged or waited for, and being ignored gradually convinces them something is wrong with them personally.
